    The colimit comparison #

    For a functor G : D → Mod A, the comparison (3.6) of the manuscript says that G(T) is the filtered colimit of the modules G(U) over the finite-dimensional subrepresentations U ⊆ T: G(T) ≅ colim_{U ⊆ T, dim U < ∞} G(U).

    The manuscript obtains this from the fact that its three functors commute with filtered colimits. Here we argue in the other direction. The comparison is checked on elements (isComparison_of_elements): every element of G(T) comes from some G(U), and an element of G(U) that vanishes in G(T) already vanishes in G(U') for a larger finite-dimensional U'. The comparison identifies G with the extension of its restriction to D_fin by filtered colimits (isoExtension), so G commutes with filtered colimits and arbitrary direct sums when it is exact, and preserves the dimension of infinite-dimensional modules when it is faithful with finite-dimensional values on D_fin.
